title: Catalog request orchestration and enterprise contract lane
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define and implement a repeatable orchestration lane for enterprise model requests that ties contractual commitments (SLA/uptime/throughput) to a prioritized intake path. This ticket covers policy, routing rules, and the annotated eval gateway that automatically assigns an intake to either 'Contracted Enterprise Lane' (requires direct PM+Sales coordination and SLA negotiation) or 'Self-Serve Catalog Lane' (standard onboarding + automated eval checks). Goal: reduce TTF (time-to-first-serving) for enterprise customers while preserving safety/compatibility gates and auditability.
comments: 2026-02-12 — Aisha Patel: Kickoff notes: initial problem statement and outline. Observed multiple incoming enterprise model requests lacking consistent priority signals and SLA context; this causes ad-hoc handoffs between PM, Sales, and Eng.

2026-02-19 — Miguel Ramirez: Drafted proposed lane rules. Core signal: customer contract clause + expected concurrent QPS -> triggers Contracted lane. Also proposed a size threshold (model > 20B params or custom RLHF) to force manual review.

2026-02-25 — Eng review (Rohit Kapoor): Concern: Contracted lane will require capacity reservation hooks in Dedicated product. Marked dependency on ENG-27310 for reservation API. Suggested adding a default fallthrough to a compatibility shadow-run for 72 hours.
2026-03-02 — Design input (Dana Schultz): UX for intake form; added a mandatory 'business impact' dropdown and 'regulatory classification' field to capture compliance needs for Private lane.

2026-03-04 — Legal/Sales sync (Lena Park): Contract templates reviewed; we need explicit SLA template variants (Throughput, Latency, Data Isolation) and a handshake protocol for pinning model versions during negotiation.
2026-03-08 — PM review (Aisha): Incorporated feedback; created annotated eval gateway doc and rollout plan. Planned canary with 2 pilot customers (one fintech, one healthcare partner).
2026-03-10 — Miguel: Wrote acceptance criteria and added links to draft Confluence RFC and intake form prototype. Starting implementation of routing rules in intake lambda.
decisions: Split intake into 2 primary lanes: 'Contracted Enterprise Lane' (human-in-the-loop, SLA negotiation, reserved capacity) and 'Self-Serve Catalog Lane' (automated eval gates + standard onboarding).
Annotated eval gateway will run a lightweight compatibility + quality check (sanity prompts, latency estimate, quantization compatibility) and produce a scored report attached to the intake record.

Version-pinning policy during contract negotiation: allow temporary pin on a specific model revision for the duration of the contract term, with scheduled migration windows and deprecation notice responsibilities documented in the contract template.
Require an explicit 'customer impact' field on intake forms; high-impact requests route to Priority Review within 48h.
Pilot approach: two 6-week pilots (one healthcare, one fintech) with measurement of TTF, number of handoffs, and SLA compliance as primary KPIs.
acceptance_criteria: Intake form update deployed: collects contract marker, expected QPS, regulatory requirements, business impact, and model technical metadata (architecture, param count, tokenizer).
Routing rules implemented in intake service: contract marker + QPS > threshold -> Contracted lane; otherwise Self-Serve unless flagged by reg or biz impact.
Annotated eval gateway integrated into Self-Serve lane and produces a PDF/JSON report summarizing compatibility, expected tail-latency, quantization readiness, and a pass/fail recommendation.
Contract templates (Throughput/Latency/Data Isolation) drafted and reviewed by Legal and Sales and stored in Confluence. Linkable from the intake record.
Two pilot customers onboarded via Contracted lane; metrics collected and dashboard established (TTF, handoffs, SLA-violations).
Runbook for PM/SE handoffs documented, including required artifacts for handover to Eng (eval report, pin request, expected QPS, compliance check list).
